dissented.finding: A real Python warning is two lines - a header and a source echo. The pattern matches the header and skips it; the echo matches nothing and is returned as the fault.
dissented.consequence: Driven end to end, the starting session is told the cause is the echoed source line while the true fault is discarded. The sole fixture uses the one-line form, which is the only warning shape where the fix works. Two further defeats: a fault line beginning with a traceback frame marker is dropped, and a multi-line refusal returns its trailing pointer instead of its reason.
dissented.what_would_have_defeated_this_finding: a fixture using the ordinary two-line warning

dissented.claim_defeated: a refusal reason reaches the session
dissented.finding: The new exception carries the reason code correctly, but no printing path reads that attribute - both stringify the failure and take the last line.
dissented.consequence: With multi-line detail the reason code is gone from the output entirely. All four cases for this use empty or single-line stderr, so none can see it.
dissented.what_would_have_defeated_this_finding: printing the attribute the new exception was created to carry

residuals.finding: The provenance guard covers only the degraded path. The success path, which normally runs, still names a session with no qualification and is byte-identical to the previous commit, so the prior witness's exact attack still yields an unqualified naming of a session the console never issued. The word is gone; the assertion structure is not. Every case for this stubs the briefing to fail, so none drives the success path.

The entry point still hedges over knowable truth when holding a typed refusal: the console answered and refused, nothing committed, and it reports that whether anything committed is unknown. The same commit fixes exactly this hedge one path over.
A genuine key error now reports as a bare key name; the type is lost because the fallback fires only on a blank message. Not false, but less diagnosable, and uncovered.
The test helper installs a module in the global module table and never removes it - the one global the repaired file still mutates without restoring. Harmless today.
